summary: PASS for the reviewed host-rendered UI only. All three initial readability findings are closed in fresh captures. Shared RF frequency/history rendering now has readable axes, units and peak labels. Physical LilyGO GUI, live data acquisition, motion and earlier RF-image fidelity remain NOT TESTED.
review_scope: Rendered local PNG evidence; production/assets read-only. No browser or device control.

reference.available: User's written design clarification: deep black/graphite, plum/pink/violet accents, legible instrument graphs, compact information panels, actual module data, encoder control.
reference.unavailable: Earlier RF reference image is absent from accessible attachments; no pixel comparison claimed. Home is outside the supplied new contact sheets.

evidence.provenance: HOST SIMULATION / PREVIEW fixtures; not screenshots from LilyGO and not real detected networks/cards/signals.
evidence.shared_renderer: Lists, radioResults, rfidCard and rfGraph frequency/RSSI-history use shared C++ pixels. Production rf_CC1101_rssi calls rfGraph. Keyboard, confirmation and status blocks are extracted from production by the preview tool.
evidence.reconstructions: RF PULSE TIMING, square wave and terminal preview are manual reconstructions, excluded from production-geometry acceptance. Pulse timing is no longer named as a frequency spectrum.
evidence.source_manifest_note: At retry, capture hashes and renderer-header source hashes all match. The only source-hash drift is src/modules/rf/rf_spectrum.cpp; root disclosed a post-capture range-data reset change. Root will regenerate the manifest/captures after production freeze. This review does not certify that later final manifest.

findings.requirement: Legible compact information panels and polished dialogs on 320x170.
findings.evidence: PREVIEW_dark-sakura_dialog_320x170.png (also Dawn/Monochrome): normal word 'screen?' splits into 'scree' and 'n?' on the next otherwise empty line.
findings.location: include/delta/widgets.h:106 messageLines; production confirmation calls it from src/core/display.cpp.
findings.impact: Character-based wrapping interrupts ordinary language and makes short confirmations harder to scan.
findings.smallest_correction: Wrap on the last fitting whitespace; use hard wrapping only when a single token exceeds the line width. Preserve explicit newlines and all characters.
findings.reproduction: Regenerate the existing dialog fixture and inspect its second line. Add a tiny runnable check for a fitting multiword string and an oversized token.
findings.resolution: Fresh dialog captures in all three themes place the whole word 'screen?' on line two; no split inside that word. messageLine regression assertions exist for whitespace wrapping and an oversized token (inspected, not run by visual reviewer).

findings.requirement: Wi-Fi must be a functional analyzer of networks and signal levels; BLE must clearly show device characteristics using actual data.
findings.evidence: PREVIEW_dark-sakura_wifi_320x170.png and PREVIEW_dark-sakura_ble_320x170.png: the AP/CHANNEL and RSSI SNAPSHOT histograms have bars but no channel or dBm bin labels or count scale. The selected dBm value and row channels are visible separately.
findings.impact: Users cannot assign a channel/RSSI range to a bar or interpret its relative count quantitatively. The extra panel has less informational value than its instrument styling suggests.
findings.smallest_correction: Add sparse readable channel ticks (such as 1/7/14), BLE bin range labels and a compact count maximum, or replace the histogram with labeled selected-device metadata. Keep values derived from the scan snapshot; no synthetic history.
findings.reproduction: Use current Wi-Fi channels 6/11/6 and BLE -73/-48/-91 fixture; verify each occupied bin can be identified at native size.
findings.resolution: Fresh Wi-Fi histogram shows channel ticks 1/7/14 and AP/CH max 2; BLE shows -110/-68/-32+ and RSSI max 1. Sparse labels fit without overlap and identify the bins/count scale at native size.

findings.requirement: Preserve readability on the physical compact display across supported themes.
findings.evidence: Sakura Dawn muted text over the selected-row focus fill measures 4.08:1 after RGB565 quantization. Main text/focus is 9.27:1. This affects selected radio metadata and values rather than intentionally disabled controls.
findings.impact: Small secondary values have weaker contrast than the 4.5:1 normal-text review threshold.
findings.smallest_correction: Slightly darken Dawn muted text, or use the primary text token for secondary values when their row is selected.
findings.reproduction: Calculate RGB565-decoded relative luminance for muted (105,88,101) against focus (222,199,211); inspect selected Wi-Fi/Settings values in the fresh Dawn capture.
findings.resolution: Dawn muted token changed to (98,78,93). Recomputed after RGB565 quantization: muted/focus 4.82:1, muted/background 6.29:1. Fresh Dawn selected metadata is darker and unobstructed.

passed_observations: Dark Sakura uses deep graphite with restrained pink/plum focus treatment; tool panels are visually distinct from the artistic Home direction described by the user.
Wi-Fi and BLE combine three compact result rows with selected RSSI and metadata; RFID presents a card surface, UID and protocol fields. They are not reduced to plain text lists.
Visible list selection has both a filled surface and an accent marker; checked/toggle states use shape as well as color.
Long file names and title strings use ellipsis without visible overlap. Folder icons, values and actions remain aligned.
Masked keyboard field, caret, shifted keys, numeric/hex grids, progress, empty scan/folder and storage-error states are present and visually distinguishable in the host captures.
Quiet work backgrounds keep the Sakura artwork subordinate to content. No unrelated template panels or decorative content were observed.
All 60 refreshed native captures match their manifest SHA256 and are exactly 320x170; 60 corresponding 4x images exist.

Shared RF frequency-bin and RSSI-history plots show a visible data trace, subtle grid, -20/-50/-80/-110 RSSI scale, frequency endpoints or chronological direction, measured-sample count, and labeled peak. Fresh Dark Sakura, Dawn and Monochrome captures show no visible clipping or overlap.
